$comment: Aircraft landing gear library.
HOW THIS LIBRARY IS BUILT — read data/SOURCES.md section 5 before using it.
AUTHORITATIVE, taken verbatim from primary sources:
gear designation, wheelbase, main gear OUTER width, MTOW    FAA Aircraft
Characteristics Database
tire size, tire pressure, maximum design taxi weight        manufacturer ACAP
percent of gross weight on the main gear (95 %)             FAA AC 150/5320-6G, G.1.3
DERIVED, exactly, from the above:
tire overall diameter / section width / rim   from the three-part designation
main gear TRACK (centreline to centreline)    from the FAA outer width:
track = outerWidth - (wheelsAcross - 1) * dualSpacing - sectionWidth
The FAA field is explicitly 'distance between outer tires in the main landing
gear' — an OUTSIDE dimension, not the centreline tread. Conflating the two
would put every main wheel in the wrong place, so the track is always derived
rather than assumed to equal it.
CROSS-CHECKED: with the dual spacings recorded here, that derivation
reproduces each manufacturer's separately published tread to within a few
centimetres on all four aircraft. test/run.mjs asserts this.
ASSUMED, and declared as such on every unit in `assumedFields`:
tandem spacing (2D and 3D gears), and nose gear dual spacing.
Nothing in the sources above constrains them. Set them from FAARFIELD
before using this app's output for pavement work — the app recomputes the
track when you change a dual spacing, so the authoritative outer width is
preserved whatever you enter.
